title: Migration 60 — a batch may only be attached to a farm you have a claim to
description: Both farmer policies decided ownership with `(created_by = auth.uid()) OR has_farm_membership(farm_id)`. The first branch tests a column ON THE ROW BEING WRITTEN, and the writer chooses that value -- so naming yourself as created_by satisfied it whatever farm_id said, and the farm test was never reached. A farmer could attach stock to a rival's farm, whose real members then saw stock they did not create. Measured on staging by migration 59's VERIFY section F, which was written to pin the gap rather than describe it. A self-referential predicate is not a permission check; it asks the caller to vouch for themselves. Replaced by has_farm_claim(farm_id): member of the farm OR its creator -- the same union the application already uses in getFarmerScope. BOTH branches are load-bearing: membership alone would lock out the creator of a brand-new farm, because NOTHING in this system writes a farm_memberships row; creator alone would lock out every co-worker. SECURITY DEFINER because an inline EXISTS on public.farms would run under the caller's RLS and reintroduce the lockout through the back door. Only the WITH CHECK clauses change -- USING keeps its created_by branch, so nobody loses a row they already hold; the hole was about which farm a row may attach TO. VERIFY proves the hole is shut (D, E) AND that nobody is locked out (B, C), with C asserting the creator has no membership row first, so it cannot pass via the wrong branch. NOT read-only; wrapped in BEGIN..ROLLBACK.

verify.note: B and C are the lockout guards and matter as much as D and E: a permission fix that refuses the people it was meant to serve is not a fix. C first ASSERTS the creator has no farm_memberships row, so it cannot pass through the membership branch and silently prove nothing -- the same vacuity trap fixture 58 fell into. The member and the creator are deliberately DIFFERENT users on DIFFERENT farms, so neither branch can mask the other. E is separate from D because WITH CHECK governs the row as it will exist, so an UPDATE re-pointing farm_id is the same attack with an extra step, and a fix applied to INSERT alone would leave it open. F pins that migration 59's NULL-safety survived.
